faq.a: It is a thin, see-through sheet of coloured plastic. You lay it over a page and read the words through it.
There is no right colour. Try a few and pick the one that feels most comfy. A grown-up can help you test them.
asks: What is the best overlay colour?

faq.q: What if an overlay does not help me?
faq.a: That is completely fine. Overlays help some people and not others. There are lots of other tools, like using your finger or bigger print.
asks: Overlays do not work for me

faq.a: No. Scientists have tested them, and the results are mixed. Some readers like them, and many find they make no difference. So try one and see.

faq.q: Can I change the colours on a screen?
faq.a: Yes. Many tablets, computers and e-readers let you change the background colour, the text size and the font. Ask a grown-up to help you find the settings.
asks: How do I change screen colours?

facts: A coloured overlay is a see-through coloured sheet laid over a page.
Research on coloured overlays has mixed results: some readers prefer them, but studies do not show that they help everyone.

quiz.say: What should you do if an overlay does not help?
quiz.show: If an overlay does not help…

options.show: Skip it and try other tools
options.say: Skip it and try other tools

quiz.why: Overlays help some people and not others, so try other tools instead.

wrong.1: If it does not help, there is no need to keep using it.

quiz.why: An overlay is a see-through coloured sheet you lay over the page.

wrong.1: An overlay goes on top of a book, but it is not a book.
